steps.title: AUTOMATED PROOF GENERATION FOR RUST CODE VIA SELF-EVOLUTION

core_judgments: The most significant contribution lies in tackling the novel and impactful task of verifying Rust code with LLMs—a task for which there is little prior work or available data, and the authors are commended for their data collection efforts.

While the task itself is new, the technical approach—bootstrapping finetuning by interleaving it with search—closely resembles the established 'expert iteration' framework (Polu et al., 2022), and the paper may overstate the novelty of its 'SAFE' method.
The truly novel aspects of the work are the specific application to Rust verification, the use of finetuning on repair tasks to improve generation, and the metric for filtering specification samples.

conclusion: The central contribution of this paper is the SAFE framework: a two-stage, self-evolving pipeline that (i) automatically synthesizes multi-level training data (specifications and proofs) for Verus-verified Rust programs by bootstrapping from GPT-4o and verifier-based filtering, and (ii) iteratively fine-tunes open-source LLMs to perform both proof generation and self-debugging using incorrect proofs and error messages. Prior work already covers key subpieces of this space: Baldur (First et al., 2023) fine-tunes LLMs for whole-proof generation and proof repair from error messages; Yao et al. (2023), Selene (Zhang et al., 2024), and AutoVerus (Yang et al., 2024) use GPT-class models and verifier feedback to synthesize and iteratively repair Verus or similar proofs; and SpecGen (Ma et al., 2024) and Clover (Sun et al., 2023) generate and filter specifications with verifier-driven feedback. However, none of these works implements a multi-round, GPT-bootstrapped self-evolving loop that jointly (a) constructs large, automatically filtered, multi-level Verus datasets from mostly unannotated Rust, and (b) uses them to train an open model with an explicit self-debugging objective. This integrated, self-evolution-based training pipeline for Rust/Verus remains unchallenged and appears genuinely new. Overall, the paper represents a genuine advance in novelty.
